hypothesis: Repeated Python process imports to check a prepared kernel venv dominate production kernel provisioner ensure time.
approach: Memoize runtime-ready probes with a content identity of installed rlm and dill plus installed interpreter and bootstrap version, preserving out-of-band repair; success-only process-global memo (cap 16 entries), a separate dill import probe on the managed-path memo miss, the direct un-memoized RLM-only probe on the custom PRIME_AGENT_KERNEL_PYTHON override path, and invalidation on every failed kernel start so the provisioner retry re-probes and rebuilds; fast-path cold/restore/restart in bootstrap/venv.rs, manager/startup.rs, provisioner.rs.
parity_notes: Custom PRIME_AGENT_KERNEL_PYTHON retains base semantics (direct RLM-only probe, no dill gate, not memoized): kernel-only cells print(1+1) and persisted x=12 verified on a dill-free custom venv on base AND candidate at this head. Auto-managed kernel venv probes dill on memo miss and repairs installed rlm/dill damage at the next first start (heal-before-start), then snapshot restore/kill-restart complete; base (no dill check anywhere) starts the kernel and fails later at snapshot time - a disclosed behavioral improvement, not a parity cut. Memo blind spot: the key covers interpreter + installed rlm + dill trees; any other site-packages damage the probe import closure touches is fingerprint-invisible, surfaces as a failed kernel start, the memo is invalidated, the retry re-probes and rebuilds - the same end state as base, one start attempt apart. Probe import closure (rlm, rlm.mcp, rlm.harness, rlm.bash, rlm.repl) has module-level imports that are stdlib or rlm-relative (httpx2/dill fn-local), adversarially re-verified at the current head; not mechanically enforced (a hermetic closure-freeze test is a suggested follow-up). The memo is process-global per daemon process: a fresh daemon cold-starts with an empty memo, so the win class is warm restarts and second sessions in the same daemon. Frozen RLM API/wire/session replay untouched; Linux x86_64 measured, macOS unmeasured, Windows layout handled (Lib/site-packages no-layer witness) but unshipped.
